_meta.verify_note: Platforms change limits and truncation points without notice. Treat these numbers as a working baseline and verify them in the platform's own ad or publishing preview before a large spend or a launch.
_meta.notes: limit = hard maximum the platform accepts (null when there is none). visible = characters a reader sees before truncation or a fold (null when not truncated). Units are characters unless a note says pixels. confidence: high = stable and widely documented, medium = varies by device, placement or test.

rsa-headline.notes: Up to 15 headlines, 3 shown at a time. Each must stand alone in any order.

rsa-description.notes: Up to 4 descriptions, 2 shown. Description 1 often appears alone on mobile.

rsa-path.notes: Two optional path fields after the display URL domain.

pmax-headline.notes: Short headlines. Performance Max needs at least 3 and allows up to 15.

pmax-description.notes: One short description of 60 characters is required, others up to 90.

business-name.notes: Shown with the logo in several formats.

primary-text.notes: Feed placements cut the text near 125 characters behind 'See more'. Put the hook and the offer before that point.

headline.notes: Recommended 27 to 40 characters. Longer headlines get cut, mostly on mobile.

description.notes: Often hidden on mobile placements. Never rely on it.

post.notes: The feed cuts the post near 210 characters behind 'see more' on desktop, and shorter on mobile. The first two lines are the hook.

ad-intro.notes: 150 characters recommended to avoid truncation in sponsored content.

ad-headline.notes: Often cut after about 70 characters, depending on format.

post.notes: Links count as 23 characters. Most non-Latin scripts count double.

caption.notes: The feed shows about 125 characters before 'more'. Up to 30 hashtags allowed.
Only the first line or two shows before 'more'. The limit has changed several times.

title.notes: Search and mobile results cut near 60 characters. Front-load the subject.

description.notes: About the first 100 characters show above the fold. Put the link or hook there.

pin-title.notes: Feed view shows roughly the first 40 characters.

pin-description.notes: Only the first 50 to 60 characters show in the feed. Keywords first.

subject-desktop.notes: Desktop clients show around 60 characters, some more.

subject-mobile.notes: Phones show roughly 30 to 40 characters. Put the point first.

preheader.notes: Inbox preview text shows around 40 to 130 characters depending on the client. Aim for 40 to 90.

from-name.notes: Cut at about 25 characters on mobile.

title.notes: Google truncates by pixel width (about 580 px), so roughly 55 to 60 characters. Wide letters cut earlier.

meta-description.notes: About 155 characters on desktop (about 920 px), around 120 on mobile. Google may rewrite it.

url-slug.notes: Short and readable. Truncated in results.

h1.notes: No hard rule. Keep it as a claim a reader can take in at a glance.

og-title.notes: Cut around 60 to 90 characters depending on the network.

og-description.notes: Facebook shows about 110 to 200; LinkedIn and Slack differ.

gsm-segment.notes: One segment in the GSM alphabet. Longer messages split into 153-character segments and cost more.

unicode-segment.notes: One emoji or non-GSM character drops the whole message to 70 per segment (67 when split).

title.notes: iOS shows roughly 40 characters, Android about 40 to 65.

body.notes: Around 110 to 130 characters show before the cut on a lock screen. Front-load the reason to open.

ios-promo-text.notes: Can be changed without a new release.

cta.notes: Two to four words. Past about 25 characters buttons wrap or shrink on mobile.
